sentences.text: This predator reached a length of 7.9 to 8 meters, stood 2.4 meters tall, and had a mass of 1500 kilograms.
Its skull features a jugal bone with a straight lower edge rather than a curved one, and a high front branch situated beneath the eye socket.
The surangular bone displays a deep oval excavation at the rear along with four rear foramina, a trait seen in few other theropods.
A distinct groove extends along the joint line between the surangular and prearticular bones.
The front neck vertebra includes an extra opening that excavates the parapophysis, the lower point of rib contact.
The fossils assigned to this species represent at least three individuals of different sizes.
Excavations for the Japan-Thailand Dinosaur Project occurred between 2007 and 2009 at the village of Saphan Hin in Nakhon Ratchasima Province.
The species Siamraptor suwati was named and described in 2019 by Duangsuda Chokchaloemwon, Soki Hattori, Elena Cuesta, Pratueng Jintasakul, Masateru Shibata, and Yoichi Azuma.
The generic name combines "Siam", the former name of Thailand, and the Latin word raptor meaning "robber".
The holotype specimen NRRU-F01020008 was found in the Aptian-aged Khok Kruat Formation.
Siamraptor has generally been classified as a member of Carcharodontosauria.
In 2026, Hattori and colleagues provisionally referred two partial braincases from the Khok Kruat Formation to Siamraptor, the only named carcharodontosaur from that formation.
Siamraptor lived during the mid-Cretaceous, between 120 and 112 million years ago in the Aptian stage, in what is now Asia.
Specific dating places its existence from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian.
In a 2024 review, Cau recovered Siamraptor as a tetanuran outside the Orionides and as a close relative of Siamotyrannus.

According to Ezcurra and Agnolin, the existence of Siamraptor would indicate that Laurasian landmasses were connected until the Barremian, though its basal position does not strictly rule out early isolation.
